key_insight: The paper argues that many video generation failures are not just model weaknesses, but a data coverage problem: training videos rarely show enough viewpoint-induced appearance change. By correcting this gap, models can learn more geometrically consistent motion under camera movement.
problem_solved: It addresses geometric inconsistency in generated videos, where scenes warp, parallax breaks, and camera motion turns into abrupt shot-like transitions instead of smooth viewpoint changes.
method: Identifies that web-scale video datasets are biased toward static or weakly moving cameras with object motion, leaving sparse supervision for camera-induced geometry changes.
Proposes a geometry-focused learning strategy to better teach models how appearance should change under viewpoint shifts.
Uses this corrected supervision to improve structural consistency across frames during camera motion.
impact: This matters because practitioners building video generation systems often struggle with unstable scene geometry even when realism looks strong frame-by-frame. Better geometric learning can improve camera control, view consistency, and overall video coherence.

paper_title: Learning to Correct Geometry in Generated Videos
